profile.campus: Austin, Travis County, Texas (CyrusOne AUS3 building)
profile.reading:
Per a datacenterHawk listing dedicated to the AUS3 site code, corroborated by CyrusOne's own 2016 press release referring to an "Austin III Data Center" and by CyrusOne's own AUS2-AUS3 campus page, this building sits at 7100 Metropolis Drive, Austin, TX, on the shared 242,000 sq ft / 19MW AUS2-AUS3 campus.

CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten; the company was acquired by ABRY Partners in 2007, purchased by Cincinnati Bell for $525 million in 2010, completed an IPO in 2013, and was taken private again in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it for approximately $15 billion. The Dallas-Fort Worth metro is anchored by CyrusOne's Carrollton (DFW1) facility, which Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry describes the company itself calling the largest data center in Texas when it opened in 2012, and today spans additional DFW-numbered buildings in Allen and Lewisville; Texas's absence of a state corporate income tax and its position as a major interstate fiber crossroads have helped make the state, alongside Northern Virginia, one of CyrusOne's largest concentrations of US facilities.

In 2016, CyrusOne purchased the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's original Aurora, Illinois data center from CME Group for roughly $130 million, with CME Group continuing to operate its Globex matching engine on site under a 15-year lease, a transaction illustrating the sale-leaseback and anchor-tenant financing structures common among large colocation operators. Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued to expand its US footprint, including the January 2025 groundbreaking of a new fifth San Antonio campus (SAT5-SAT6) representing roughly $1 billion in cumulative San Antonio capital investment per the company's own materials, indicating continued growth investment in Texas markets under private ownership rather than a slowdown following the take-private transaction.

reading.body:
The CyrusOne Austin Data Center III has no confirmed individual power capacity recorded, only a note that the Austin campus as a whole publishes 19 MW of IT capacity.

CyrusOne operates this facility as a privately held company following its 2022 acquisition by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners for approximately 15 billion dollars. The facility sits on Metropolis Drive in Travis County alongside a neighboring data center, both part of a multi-building campus. The company holds relevant security certifications including SSAE 16, HIPAA, and FISMA, indicating the facility serves regulated workloads.

The absence of a facility-specific power figure limits visibility into how much compute this building actually supports. The published 19 MW for the entire Austin campus does not tell whether this third building carries most of that load or a small fraction. For tracking the binding constraint of power on AI scaling, individual facility capacity matters more than campus totals.

The ownership shift to private equity in 2022 means this facility no longer reports performance data to public markets. The CME Group transaction history shows how critical individual data center locations can be for financial infrastructure, but provides no current detail on whether this Austin building serves similar mission-critical tenants or the types of workloads it now hosts.
